notes.title: Murderous Muses Case Files board game available now!
notes.content:
Break out of the gallery and hit the streets to investigate Mordechai's murder as you've never investigated it before! Murderous Muses Case Files game is a tabletop spin-off of your favourite 2023 FMV whodunit, that lets you take over where Mirlhaven's police department gave up. 

Get your detective on with unfettered access to the original suspect interview transcripts, crime scene report and witness statements. Scour these files and more for clues, then use the Mirlhaven Directory to follow up leads. Take a trip to the crime scene, the coroners, the docks, the spooky Undulating Hills and question new islanders along the way!

Perfect to play on your own or with friends, Murderous Muses Case Files immerses you further into the details of the case and plunges you firsthand into the uncanny lore of Mirlhaven. With over 100 residents, businesses and landmarks to choose from, you’ll need sharp investigative skills to stay on the trail of the killer. Of course, there’s nothing to stop you taking a tour of the whole island, if curiosity gets the better of you…

Unlike the videogame, there’s only one solution to Murderous Muses Case Files but you'll still need to rule out each suspect until only the killer remains!

notes.title: Murderous Muses is Out Now!
notes.content:
After almost 2 years in development, Murderous Muses is launching today!

Spend three nights in a haunted art gallery solving the murder of Mordechai Grey - a devilish artist killed by one of his six muses. Explore the ever-changing rooms and corridors to uncover clues, find collectibles, and piece together the layered narrative to find out whodunit - and why.

[previewyoutube=7XIBNT2ANVc;full][/previewyoutube]

You've been hired as the new night watch at Gallery Argenta. But as soon as you start your shift, the gallery changes, revealing mysterious exhibitions full of talking paintings, puzzling words and locked rooms. Hanging paintings in these night galleries reveals Mordechai's memories, but can you use what you uncover to find out who killed him?

Murderous Muses Features
[list]
[*] Solve a murder mystery that re-rolls every time you play
[*] A rich new story setting, Mirlhaven island
[*] Explore a procedurally-generated gallery and share seeds with friends
[*] Puzzles unlock bonus treasure rooms
[*] A persistent ‘trophy room’ to store collectibles
[*] Final score cards and run times for bragging rights
[/list]

notes.title: Steam Deck Compatibility
notes.content:
We've created a special Linux port of Murderous Muses including webm (not mp4) videos so that everything plays as smoothly as possible. Cloud saves work between PC, Mac and Steam Deck.

The touchscreen has been disabled so we've included a pop-up keyboard for seed entry (the only place in the game it's needed) but other than that it's the same codebase as PC and shares all the same features.

notes.title: Feature Spotlight - The Eyes of Mordechai
notes.content:
In Murderous Muses, you catch the killer by seeing through the eyes of victim Mordechai Grey. But how exactly do you do that? Well, in this third feature spotlight, we're going to show you! 

Presenting…. the Eyes of Mordechai!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/8f93e6d48f7324dfc3f8cea678c48f04dc090acf.gif[/img]

The Eyes of Mordechai are like miniature crystal balls. Each one allows you to see into the past, restoring Mordechai's memories of his conversations with the six prime suspects - a.k.a. his Murderous Muses.

Every night, the painting frames are newly socketed with 6 eyes. Every time you play a painting on a keyword it consumes one eye, so you should choose carefully what to reveal. If you run out of eyes, you won’t be able to unlock all the police interviews, and they’re crucial for solving the murder!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/1c4f3d42c63f65937e9ec00fc11ac570c7dbccd5.gif[/img]

The good news is, you can use restoration tables to move eyes between paintings - which will be a big help if you’ve accidentally squandered them all chasing down Otto and Pip’s jokes, or if you want to head down the rabbit hole with Lilith. The bad news is, you only get one eye for every two you recycle...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/0e949ae88a16947dc0b41948199dd11ccdf6b9a5.gif[/img]

The Eyes of Mordechai will also come in handy if you want to avail yourself of the in-game Tips Hotline. Who knows where the operators get their info from, but the word on the street says they can help you rule out one of the innocent suspects…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/a32cceaa86653d1500de5135229850e6e4706cd5.gif[/img]

You can also earn an achievement for solving the murder with 20 eyes leftover in your inventory. Think you could do it? Wishlist Murderous Muses here!

notes.title: Feature Spotlight - The Gallery with a Mind of its Own
notes.content:
In Murderous Muses, you play as the night watch exploring a reality-shifting gallery to solve a murder. In this second feature spotlight, we’re taking a closer look all the different ways the gallery elements are “re-rolled” each time you play...

By day, Gallery Argenta is just a normal gallery. You can wander the exhibit and help your boss Sasha hang paintings ready for the grand opening. But as soon as you start your night shift, things take a turn for the spooky - not least because an haunting presence is watching your every move!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/41b0d1d5ce34330df74bf2073b0d2db6935364da.gif[/img]

Beyond the familiar walls of reception, new galleries spawn in random, unexpected ways. In each one, you’ll discover an exhibit populated with mysterious keywords on which you can hang portraits of the suspects. We procedurally generate the keywords and arrangement in which they appear, so each player experiences the game in a different way.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/c64736782de22af796fb3e7c02318920021683bd.gif[/img]

Other elements are shuffled too - from the way the galleries connect and the locations of hidden objects, to the clues you’re shown about the murder and memory mini-games you can play. Solving the mini-game puzzles is optional but can “urn” you collectibles which - you’ve guessed it! - are randomly spawned in locked treasure rooms.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/16392e76677e69fb398a21b66a7ca074f85d095c.gif[/img]

Murderous Muses has been built from the ground up to be infinitely re-playable so, like Cluedo, the murderer can be any of the suspects in each playthrough. You can’t tell whodunit without using deduction (even if you’re one of the devs playing for the 100th time!) 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/9cb9082bab40f2bbadda90b5be1099ab69381e8c.gif[/img]

Not only does each game give you a fresh gameboard to play on and explore, but you can share seeds with your friends and try to beat each other’s scores. And every time you play, you’ll uncover more about Mordechai Grey, his ‘Murderous Muses’ and the mysterious island setting of Mirlhaven…

Murderous Muses is releasing soon so wishlist now to get it on launch day!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1727270/Murderous_Muses/

notes.title: Feature Spotlight - Mirlhaven's Unsolved Mysteries
notes.content:
With the release date for Murderous Muses looming, we’re taking the opportunity to highlight some of the gameplay features you’ll encounter when you take over as the night watch for Gallery Argenta. First up - Mirlhaven’s Unsolved Mysteries!

With all the uncanny events on the island, it’s no surprise Mirlhaven has its very own unsolved mysteries TV show. And the greatest unsolved mystery of all surrounds the murder of controversial artist Mordechai Grey. 

Every night when the gallery changes, you’ll be able to view a clip from the show revealing a different piece of evidence. How, exactly, was the victim killed? Where did the culprit obtain the murder weapon? What trace evidence was left at the scene? And who placed a mysterious call to the doomed artist on the morning of his murder...?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/e6ede74da459d73022e65420488fc248566c0836.gif[/img]

With nine separate clues to follow up, you'll explore the gallery to search for related threads, hanging the suspects on plaques to restore the victim's memories. Each of the portraits has a limited number of uses though so you'll need to choose carefully if you want to uncover which of the Murderous Muses is guilty!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/36c7d76ba9ba81c79881f8832ddc293f85e2995b.gif[/img]

Whatever your investigation turns up, you won’t be able to eliminate suspects completely without unlocking their police interviews - which is a puzzle in itself. We'll say more about that soon, but until then wishlist Murderous Muses here!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1727270/Murderous_Muses/

notes.title: FMV fan favourites join the Murderous Muses cast!
notes.content:
Murderous Muses has entered the final stages of development, which means we're busy testing, tweaking and touching up the scenery ready for release in just a few months. It won't be long until we have a full trailer to show you and - fingers crossed - a release date announcement! 

But before that, we've got some final, exciting, cast members to reveal. We're thrilled to announce the return of some familiar faces (and voices) to the D'Avekki Studios fold, this time helping us add mystery and intrigue to the 3D gallery as you explore...

[h2]The Gallery Speaks![/h2]
First up, we’ve been enhancing the strange and otherworldly atmosphere of the gallery, courtesy of voice over artists Ayvianna Snow and Will Harrison-Wallace. If you've played Dark Nights with Poe and Munro, you'll probably recognise Ayvianna as Millicent from the second episode, “In Bed with Poe and Munro”.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/edc91697c11f747863eec1910dc6c26b73b838e9.gif[/img]

Ayvianna plays J.A.M.I.E., your Jovial Art Museum Information Educator and day gallery narrator, who reveals Mirlhaven's local lore when you place paintings in their correct positions.

Will joins us for the first time as Higgins, the gallery’s former security guard, who witnessed some strange occurrences and added his own theories to the night gallery. He’s also got plenty to say on other matters, including your attempts at puzzle solving, and he might have left you a few notes lying around too.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/9eb983feacaca671410f4671fee47fbdfb8ba81c.png[/img]

[h2]From Radio to TV[/h2]
We’re also thrilled to welcome back Klemens Koehring, another D’Avekki regular, in the role of local expert of the unexplained, Dr Crispin Howe. Klemens played radio host John 'Poe' Pope in both The Shapeshifting Detective and Dark Nights with Poe and Munro.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/b568064380ea7774fb02172e8bc98864f0633ebe.gif[/img]

Dr Howe presents episodes of ‘Mirlhaven’s Unsolved Mysteries’... the island’s own late night documentary about everything weird and wonderful that happens there, including the murder of Mordechai Grey. There are nine episodes in total to find and each one focuses on a new piece of evidence so you won’t want to miss them!

[h2]The Booth at the End[/h2]
Finally, FMV legend Rupert Booth (Jenks in [i]Contradiction: Spot the Liar[/i] and Dupont in [i]The Shapeshifting Detective[/i]), joins Murderous Muses as the voice of Detective Salisbury.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/35dd859690171850cad921c542084fc1a2b04137.gif[/img]

If you're successful in unlocking specific memories for a suspect, you’ll be rewarded with a brief flashback of their police interview. Rupert's dulcet tones can be heard asking probing questions which reveal crucial clues about the murder so make sure you pay attention!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/77dea2e46506f11131cf46ae27e718de427cc018.png[/img]

[h2]The Paint Thickens[/h2]
Along with adding video and audio content, we've been busy furnishing the gallery with puzzles, treasure rooms and collectibles... plus a few easter eggs for you to find. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/fb45fdfe76771893769fd9025299752bc44740c1.jpg[/img]

There's even a scorecard at the end of the game so you can see how well you did - hanging paintings correctly, unlocking police interviews, solving puzzles and of course, catching the killer. It also shows you how much of the full game you’ve unlocked, which we hope will make you want to replay it (there’s so much more to discover!)

We hope you're as excited about the release of Murderous Muses as we are and we can't wait for you to explore the gallery, meet the Murderous Muses, and uncover the secrets of Mirlhaven!

notes.title: Whodunit? Unveiling Mirlhaven’s Most Wanted…
notes.content:
Filming has finished for our Murderous Muses - the six suspects you’ll meet in the FMV parts of the game - and we’re getting stuck in to editing the footage (about 600 videos!) ready to drop them into the gallery.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/2851bddf2826c097767bcac35120149fe2fbfb40.png[/img]

The murderer is selected at random at the start of each playthrough meaning any one of the six Muses could be the killer. It’s up to you to decide who’s innocent and who’s guilty based on their statements and the evidence you discover – whether that’s about the time of the murder, clues at the scene of the crime, the murder weapon, or the very specific symbol painted in blood on the victim’s forehead. It’s all very Cluedo-esque just more… occulty.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/9211dc802183373bb3daec17c677c8f58bafdc2a.png[/img]

Each suspect will also have their own sordid and/or supernatural story to reveal, and of course, they’ll each have a very good reason to want to kill poor innocent artist Mordechai Grey... 

Which Murderous Muse is your favourite? And which do you think seems the most guilty...?

notes.title: Dev update - the gallery is growing
notes.content:
Here at D'Avekki Studios, we've been busy developing Murderous Muses and thought it was time to give you an update on our progress and what you’ll be able to do in game when it releases later this year.

[h2]No Ordinary Gallery[/h2]
Over the last couple of months, Sam and Tim have been focusing hard on bringing the 3D gallery to life and giving it a mind of its own by adding randomly generated rooms, spontaneously spawning paintings and clockwork exhibits to keep you guessing. The whole game might take place inside the gallery walls, but those walls don’t always stay in the same place! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/81820bf9f520da6b3af9d5358e96dc203db5e6ed.png[/img]

[h2]The Artist's Vision[/h2]
We’ve also been fleshing out the gameplay and adding loads of things for you to explore. You can discover the otherworldly origins of Mirlhaven Island and its lore - from the Headless Hearseman to the Undulating Hills - by finding and hanging paintings. Then, as the gallery shifts, you’ll encounter strange objects and puzzles that appear overnight, allowing you to unlock secret rooms that weren’t there before. And in the mysterious night exhibition, you can use the swirling ‘Eyes of Mordechai’ to bring paintings to life and see into the past, uncovering the final weeks of the artist and his muses in glorious full motion video! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/1ff78cd4b4a295a97daf28f59a5ae368e058db08.png[/img]

[h2]Framing a Murderer[/h2]
Which brings us to the heart of the game: the murder mystery - or rather, the murder [i]mysteries[/i]. The aim of the game is to work out who killed Mordechai Grey, but we want you to be able to replay it as many times as you like, without being able to tell ‘whodunit’ until the end. This means the murder mystery elements are shuffled whenever you start a new game. The murderer will be chosen at random from one of six potential suspects, along with three framing devices - the clues you’ll use to decide which muse is guilty. You won’t be able to work out who the murderer is until you’ve seen all three frames and revealed each suspect’s connection to them, meaning you can solve the mystery time and time again with no spoilers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41309109/12d53f6112abcad2b0ccf494fa1998363994bed3.png[/img]

[h2]Sketchy Suspects[/h2]
But that’s only half the story. As well as getting to complete a murder investigation every time you play, you’ll also be unraveling parts of a much bigger puzzle, namely the secrets surrounding Mordechai Grey and his six muses. All of the suspects are very different, and each has their own tragic tale which you’ll need several playthroughs to reveal. There’s the ventriloquist who’s constantly outshone by his dummy, the criminologist pulling the strings of Mirlhaven’s most wanted, the grief-stricken burlesque dancer making all the wrong choices, the perky undertaker with a taste for the macabre, the clockmaker who’s too tightly wound for his own good, and the tennis twins desperate to escape their family curse. Tim and Lynda have been busy writing these scripts over the last couple of months and we’re getting ready to begin casting at the end of this month so watch this space!
